messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike observed on /v1/stream (hosted) across us-west-2. Aggregated SLO breach. Auto-mitigation triggered: fallback routing to small-models.
omar (eng-sre): saw a sharp jump starting ~3234567750. p95 up from 120ms -> 420ms, p99 up to 3.2s. Streaming stalls and partial responses.
elaine (eng-runtime): stack traces show many tail requests hitting prefix cache miss path. Rolling prefix-hash rollout 2026-03-10T09:00 pushed earlier today may be the cause.
chris (eng-oncall): paging alerts: prefetch workers are starved, KV miss rate increased 12x. Customer impact: several high-traffic tenants reported truncated streams. Jun any CS escalations?
jun (customer-success): one enterprise customer reported requests timing out and seeing partial tokens. They're opening a case, asked for an ETA.
omar (eng-sre): collecting traces now — linking flamegraphs and p99 request IDs. Suggest immediate mitigation: pause prefix-hash rollout and route streaming to fallback cache tier while we triage.
elaine (eng-runtime): agreed. I'm prepping a rollback of the prefix-hash feature flag. Also can increase prefetch worker parallelism and temporary TTL bump for prefetched prefixes.
chris (eng-oncall): is the fallback routing already active? incident-bot mentioned small-model fallback, but we need fallback that preserves streaming.
incident-bot: ACTION: created runbook run-3234567800. Paging: eng-runtime oncall -> elaine. SLA timer started.
omar (eng-sre): commands I'm running:
```
# quick check of prefix hit rates
curl -s "https://metrics/api/prefix_hits?since=3234567600&until=3234567800" | jq .
# increase prefetch workers
kubectl -n runtime scale deployment/prefetch-workers --replicas=12
```
elaine (eng-runtime): scaled prefetch to 12 (was 4). Increasing prefetch TTL to 30m from 5m for hot prefixes. Pushing feature-flag pause: ffctl pause prefix-hash-rollout --env=prod --reason="latency spike"
katy (eng-platform): routing change in flight: adding rule to steer streaming routes to fallback cache pool with warmed KV (region us-west-2 -> fallback-shard-a). Taking <2m to propagate.
omar (eng-sre): observed immediate drop in short-tail p95 after worker scale but p99 still heavy. Looks like tail requests that miss the cache are causing sync IO stalls.
elaine (eng-runtime): I found a regression in prefix normalization: a small subset of keys got different canonical forms after hash change, causing a namespace split. Hit rate for that namespace dropped to 3%. Going to submit hotfix to normalize canonicalization for both old/new hash.
chris (eng-oncall): customers: Jun is keeping them patched. Any ETA for rollback vs hotfix?
jun (customer-success): customer asked directly for ETA, they want a timeline. Please provide asap.
elaine (eng-runtime): pause rollout applied. Rollback of prefix-hash is risky due to partial state — hotfix faster: deploy normalization patch to read both variants for 30m window. ETA ~25min to staging validation, then +10m to prod.
omar (eng-sre): ok do hotfix first. Meanwhile, continue fallback routing and TTL bump. I'll also enable async prefetch fallback so misses don't block streams.
incident-bot: UPDATE: fallback routing completed, prefetch scaled, TTL updated. Metrics dashboard: https://dash/internal/3234567800
katy (eng-platform): FYI routing rule caused ~1% extra cost but reduced p95 by ~180ms for affected streams.
elaine (eng-runtime): pushing hotfix patch now:
```
git checkout -b fix/prefix-dual-read
# normalize + dual-read code
cargo build --release && airflow deploy runtime/prefix-normalizer --env prod
```
chris (eng-oncall): monitoring traces. Any sign of customer improvement yet?
jun (customer-success): customer confirmed partial improvement on a subset of requests, still seeing occasional timeouts. They're relieved but asking for followup.
omar (eng-sre): after hotfix deploy, prefix hit rate for the namespace climbed from 3% -> 68% within 6 minutes. p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s. Streaming stall frequency down 70%.
elaine (eng-runtime): rolling full deploy completed. Leaving dual-read mode for 1h, then schedule backfill to rekey any orphaned prefixes. Also plan to run cache rehydrate job: rehydrate --namespace broken-ns --parallel 24
chris (eng-oncall): excellent. Prepare for handoff: I'm oncall until 4pm PT, then @omar will take 4-12. Handoff note: continue to watch p99 < 1.2s and prefix-hit > 80% for the next 2 hours.
omar (eng-sre): taking handoff at 4pm. Action items for next oncall: follow up on cache rehydrate job, validate backfill completed, postpone prefix-rollout until we have canary metrics.
katy (eng-platform): will open a postmortem ticket and link rollout pipeline, enabling tighter gating on prefix normalization. Also adding a test harness for dual-hash compatibility.
jun (customer-success): I'll send a summary to impacted customers and offer a follow-up sync. They requested root cause details once postmortem is ready.
incident-bot: STATUS: mitigations decreased error volume by 92%. SLA breach window duration estimated 12m. Created handoff message and postmortem ticket PM-3234.
chris (eng-oncall): final notes before handoff:
- root cause: prefix-hash change + normalization regression -> namespace split -> low cache hit -> sync IO stalls -> p99 spike
- mitigations performed: pause rollout, scale prefetch, TTL bump, fallback routing to warmed shard, hotfix dual-read deploy, cache rehydrate plan
- customer impact: partial truncation/timeouts for high-throughput tenants, enterprise case opened, no data loss
- next steps: backfill, canary plan for re-rollout, add dual-hash unit tests, monitoring alert refinement
omar (eng-sre): thanks all. Taking over at 16:00 PT. Leaving alert thresholds lowered for additional 1h to avoid flapping.
elaine (eng-runtime): I'll follow up on backfill job and postmortem write-up with code pointers.
jun (customer-success): sending customer note now. Thanks team. :heartpulse:
chris (eng-oncall): handing off. Oncall handover complete.
incident-bot: HANDOFF: 3234567800 -> next_oncall (omar) at 3234568000. Thread closed for live ops but open for postmortem comments.
